name: use-independent-native-verifiers
reason: Preserve verifier independence and the upstream publication duties; change only forge discovery and cloud execution.
anchor: 1. **Resolve the forge, then verify each PR independently before it lands.** GitHub CLI (`gh`) is the default. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, use `origin pr` for every PR operation. Otherwise stay on `gh` and record the fallback. Never require Graphite (`gt`). One verifier per PR, each a Cursor cloud agent, runs the change the way a user would with the matching control skill (such as `control-ui` or `control-cli` from `cursor-team-kit`), parent against head, and posts `PASS`, `PASS+NOTES`, or `FAIL` on that PR. Only a verdict from an agent that did not write the code counts, because an author checks what it meant to build. Green CI and an approving bot review are not verdicts, because neither runs the change as a user would.

name: bind-shipping-to-the-request-not-the-mode
reason: The explicit shipping task supplies scope; do not add per-merge confirmation or bypass project and forge gates.
anchor: **You own what lands. Verify each PR independently, land only the verified run from the root, then keep your hands off the stack.**
find: then keep your hands off the stack.**

Use this for an operator-authorized land/ship task, not for opening, verification, babysitting or enabling the mode. Scope the named run before acting; existing host, project and forge gates still apply.

name: observe-queued-stack-within-live-session
reason: Use explicit bounded local reads, without a durable scheduler or calling a merge command from the watcher.
anchor: 5. **Leave the stack alone while it lands.** Step 4's move of the next PR is the only change to a branch or base, because a merge lands whatever its branch and base hold at that moment, verdict or not. On GitHub, watch the run with `scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr --queued-stack` under `/loop` until it reports `COMPLETE` at the ceiling. Pass the run's PR numbers, bottom-to-top, in `--stack-prs`, and pass the same list each time you restart the watcher. On Origin, re-read the current PR with `origin pr view <pr> --checks` each time `origin pr checks <pr> --watch` returns, until the ceiling reads merged. A base that moves to trunk when its parent merges is expected, not damage to repair. If a merge stalls, find out why before you change anything.
